raw_response_text:
{
  "project_id": "P-STP-YouthEmployment",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Involvement of multiple line ministries and agencies across project components may cause institutional coordination friction and implementation delays.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish a Ministerial Coordination Committee under the Minister of Labor and utilize a restructured PIU shared with SPRRP.",
      "evidence": "Section IV.B Financial Management: ...delays in preparing annual workplans and implementing interventions due to the involvement of multiple stakeholders..."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Public TVET institutions face capacity constraints due to outdated equipment, limited infrastructure, operating deficits, and instructor gaps.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Provide direct financial compensation for training delivery costs, procure modern equipment, and rehabilitate existing facilities through AFAP.",
      "evidence": "Section I.B Sectoral Context: ...capacity remains constrained by outdated equipment, limited infrastructure, insufficient operating budgets, staffing gaps..."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Construction of the US$5 million training center on Príncipe faces severe logistical constraints, cost risks, and delays due to geographic insularity.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Procure detailed technical designs early, enforce EDGE Level 1 green building standards, and manage budget adjustments through procurement plan revisions.",
      "evidence": "Section II.D Subcomponent 1.1: ...structural constraints specific to Príncipe—including geographic isolation and a severely limited pool of skilled workers..."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Financial management bottlenecks at AFAP, including transaction recording delays and late internal audit reviews, could impede project disbursements.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Appoint a dedicated financial management accountant, customize accounting software, and update the financial procedures in the Project Operations Manual.",
      "evidence": "Section IV.B Financial Management: FM risks identified include: (i) delays in recording financial transactions and generating financial reports; (ii) internal audit reviews..."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Delays in MLSSS providing technical inputs and specifications to AFAP could stall procurement of civil works, goods, and key consultancies.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish formal workflow protocols between MLSSS technical leads and AFAP fiduciary specialists, detailed in the Project Operations Manual.",
      "evidence": "Section IV.B Procurement: A key factor for good procurement performance will be the ability of AFAP and the MLSSS to work in close collaboration..."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Delays or non-compliance in beneficiary selection criteria could interrupt cash stipend and sub-grant transfers for youth and MSMEs.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Contract a qualified electronic Payment Service Provider and satisfy formal disbursement conditions prior to sub-grant and stipend releases.",
      "evidence": "Section IV.B Financial Management: ...delays in availing funds for beneficiaries resulting from possible non-compliance in selection criteria."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Vulnerable youth outside the capital or unindexed in databases face potential exclusion and elite capture during project beneficiary selection.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Utilize objective socio-economic data from the Unique Social Registry, enforce geographic quotas, and operationalize a project Grievance Redress Mechanism.",
      "evidence": "Section IV.C ESF: ...risks of exclusion, which may arise if project benefits are not equitably distributed... as well as risks of elite capture..."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Female participants in training centers, internships, and work placements face risks of sexual exploitation, abuse, and sexual harassment.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Appoint a dedicated Social Specialist with GBV/SEA-SH expertise and enforce code-of-conduct and safety mechanisms across participating training centers and employers.",
      "evidence": "Section IV.C ESF: ...community health and safety risks, including risks of sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) and sexual harassment (SH)..."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Micro-enterprise grants and facility rehabilitation works could generate solid waste, construction debris, or cause localized environmental degradation in sensitive ecosystems.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Appoint an Environmental Specialist, mandate environmental screening for MSME sub-grants, and enforce environmental management guidelines for civil works.",
      "evidence": "Section IV.C ESF: ...small business grants could support micro-enterprises in agriculture, fisheries, or tourism that may indirectly place pressure on sensitive ecosystems..."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Delays in recruiting core PIU technical staff (TVET specialist, IT assistant, E&S specialists) could overburden existing staff and slow component rollout.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Enforce legal covenants mandating the appointment of key specialists within 45 to 60 days of project effectiveness.",
      "evidence": "Legal Covenants: The Recipient shall cause AFAP to hire or appoint, not later than sixty (60) days after Effectiveness: (i) a TVET specialist..."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Recurrent flooding, storms, and sea-level rise could disrupt training activities, delay infrastructure works, and impact beneficiary livelihoods.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Apply climate-resilient engineering standards for physical works, install backup generators, and incorporate flexible training schedules.",
      "evidence": "Section IV.C Assessment of adaptation risks: ...increased frequency and severity of natural hazards and climate shocks may cause disruptions in service delivery..."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "The new digital Employability Portal and upgraded LMIS risk underutilization or power disruption, mirroring past unoperationalized labor observatory systems.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Adopt a cloud-based architecture, procure backup power systems, and contract specialized technical assistance for system development and user training.",
      "evidence": "Section II.D Subcomponent 1.2: ...an 'Employment Observatory' was previously developed with support from the ILO but never fully operationalized..."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Dominance of low-productivity informal firms in STP limits the domestic private sector's structural capacity to absorb interns into permanent wage jobs.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Combine internship schemes with self-employment startup grants, productive inclusion packages, and MSME growth support.",
      "evidence": "Section I.A Country Context: Micro and small enterprises make up 92 percent of all firms in STP... Most are household-run and provide few job opportunities."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "High youth emigration sentiment (68%) without legal structures may result in uncoordinated brain drain or precarious irregular migration outcomes.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Incorporate structured labor mobility orientation sessions, align skills with destination country demands, and support formal international labor mobility channels.",
      "evidence": "Section I.B Sectoral Context: A recent survey found that 68 percent of youth are considering leaving the country in search of better opportunities abroad..."
    }
  ]
}
